# Psalm 59 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the music director. A psalm of David, regarding the time Saul sent soldiers to watch David's house in order to kill him. To the tune of 'Do Not Destroy.'

**2** Rescue me from my enemies, O God. Protect me from those who have come to destroy me.

**3** Rescue me from these criminals; save me from these murderers.

**4** They have set an ambush for me. Fierce enemies are out there waiting, LORD, though I have not sinned or offended them.

**5** I have done nothing wrong, yet they prepare to attack me. Wake up! See what is happening and help me!

**6** O LORD God of Heaven's Armies, the God of Israel, wake up and punish those hostile nations. Show no mercy to wicked traitors. Pause and reflect.

**7** They come out at night, snarling like vicious dogs as they prowl the streets.

**8** Listen to the filth that comes from their mouths; their words cut like swords. 'After all, who can hear us?' they sneer.

**9** But LORD, You laugh at them. You scoff at all the hostile nations.

**10** You are my strength; I wait for You to rescue me, for You, O God, are my fortress.

**11** In His unfailing love, my God will stand with me. He will let me look down in triumph on all my enemies.

**12** Don't kill them, for my people soon forget such lessons; stagger them with Your power, and bring them to their knees, O Lord our shield.

**13** Because of the sinful things they say, because of the evil that is on their lips, let them be captured by their pride, their curses, and their lies.

**14** Destroy them in Your anger! Wipe them out completely! Then the whole world will know that God reigns in Israel. Pause and reflect.

**15** My enemies come out at night, snarling like vicious dogs as they prowl the streets.

**16** They scavenge for food but go to sleep unsatisfied.

**17** But as for me, I will sing about Your power. Each morning I will sing with joy about Your unfailing love. For You have been my refuge, a place of safety when I am in distress.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **59:17**: Morning comes as the counterpoint to the dogs' nighttime prowling. The psalmist sings at dawn because he has survived the night.

— PNEUMA
